info.bio:
The Specials es una banda británica de ska (más precisamente del estilo que se conoce como 2 Tone) formada en 1977 en Coventry. Junto a Madness es una de las bandas más importantes que haya dado el género. Luego de muchos años de estar separados, en 2009 han vuelto al ruedo, subidos al revival que el 2 tone y el ska esta viviendo en el mundo.

Empezaron tocando ska y punk; más tarde fusionaron todo estos estilos, creando un nuevo sonido que fue concido como 2 Tone.

scenes.name: 2-Tone: The Specials y el ska de los Midlands
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: El sello de Jerry Dammers llenó en 1979 el hueco de un punk bailable: The Specials, siete músicos blancos y negros de Coventry (Terry Hall y su mirada heredada de Rotten, el rude boy Neville Staple), cruzan el ska de Prince Buster con la energía punk y un realismo social en blanco y negro («Gangsters», «Too Much Too Young», «Concrete Jungle», «Nite Klub»). El damero blanco y negro simboliza la integración racial; The Beat (Handsworth: «Mirror in the Bathroom», «Stand Down Margaret»), The Selecter («On My Radio») y Madness suman cinco hits en cinco singles. El sueño de un «nuevo Motown» se convierte en «un monstruo»: More Specials se refugia en la música ligera y la caja de ritmos, y «Ghost Town» (1981), retrato de la desindustrialización, llega al número uno mientras arden las ciudades. Fun Boy Three, «Nelson Mandela» y el fin. Posmoderno antes del new pop: «Estamos trayendo de vuelta algo que nunca existió».

podcast.title: Two-Tone Records Founded 1979 – Black-and-White Logo Based on Peter Tosh Photo; Anti-Racist Mission
podcast.body: Jerry Dammers founded Two-Tone Records, naming it after the black-and-white suits worn by mods and skinheads of the 1960s and after the peaceful multiracial makeup of the band. The label's logo — a man in a black and white suit, white shirt, black tie, sunglasses, pork pie hat, white socks, and black loafers — was drawn by Dammers based on a photo of Peter Tosh when he was a member of the Wailers. The character was named Walt Jabsco (Walt after Walt Disney). Two-Tone had an explicit anti-racism message at a time when racial tensions in the UK were getting out of control. "Two-tone became the core of the second wave of Scott."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: A Not-So Brief History of Ska: Part 1

podcast.title: Adopting Ska for Energy
podcast.body: Finding reggae too slow for the energetic sound he aimed for, Dammers turned to ska, reggae's ancestor, which had a choppier beat akin to punk but suitable for dancing, and could convey both anger and happiness. "Now Reggae was too slow for the energy that Jerry wanted to produce, so he defaulted to Reggae's ancestor. Scott."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Advocates for Racial Harmony
podcast.body: In their performances, The Specials consistently promoted messages of racial and social harmony. "Whenever the specials played, they preached racial social harmony."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Anti-Racism Stance and Rock Against Racism
podcast.body: Dammers, growing up in a multi-racial city and witnessing racism, was inspired by the Rock Against Racism movement that started in 1978, leading him to form an inclusive band. "Growing up in a multi-racial city, he hated the racism that he saw around him and was inspired by the rock against racism movement that began in 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: British Music Press Championing
podcast.body: The Specials were a prominent band within the post-punk Ska movement and were widely championed by the British music press. "SCA was one of the big post-punk sounds thanks to bands like the Specials and the Selector and Madness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Influences
podcast.body: Formed by white keyboardist Jerry Dammers in Coventry, The Specials were deeply influenced by the music brought by West Indian immigrants to his hometown, specifically reggae, dub, rock steady, and especially ska. "They were formed by keyboardist Jerry Damors, a white kid who was entranced by all the music new West Indian immigrants had brought with them to his hometown of Coventry."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founding Two Tone Records
podcast.body: In March 1979, The Specials borrowed £700 from family and friends to establish their independent record label, Two Tone, named after the black and white suits worn by mods and skinheads in the 1960s and reflecting the band's peaceful, multi-racial lineup. "In March 1979, the Specials borrowed 700 pounds from family and friends to form an independent record label that Jerry Damors called Two Tone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Integrated Band Design
podcast.body: From its inception, The Specials were designed to be an integrated band, consistently featuring a mix of black and white musicians, including Caribbean immigrants, over the years. "From the very beginning, the specials were designed to be an integrated band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inventing the Uniform
podcast.body: Jerry Dammers created a distinctive uniform for the band, a blend of West Indian rude boy, British skinhead, and British mod styles, featuring suits, pork pie hats, dark glasses, crisp white shirts, and neat ties. "One of the things he did was invent a uniform. It was a cross between a West Indian rude boy, a British skinhead, and a British mod. This meant suits, pork pie hats, dark glasses, and crisp white shirts and neat ties."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jerry Dammers' Background and Motivation
podcast.body: Founder Jerry Dammers, born in India and the ex-hippie son of a missionary minister, was deeply influenced by the diverse music heard on the streets of Coventry. He used music to rebel against his father and to push back against the bleak working-class existence of his city, embracing punk's freedom of expression. "Jerry Damers was born in India and the ex-Hippie son of a missionary minister. He was a huge fan of all this music that he was hearing in the street. He was also very much into the freedom of expression that came with the punk movement of the 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: John Hughes Film Exposure (1980s)
podcast.body: The Specials were one of many bands whose music was heavily mined for the soundtracks of John Hughes' 1980s films. These carefully curated soundtracks played a significant role in introducing a wide audience in North America to bands from the alternative rock scene, particularly British performers. "So many people learned of bands like The Specials and Spandovalet and Billy Idle and General Public and Wang Chung and Yellow and New Order and the Psychedelic Furs and the Smiths and Echo and the Bunyman, Susanne Vagan in excess the Jesus and Mary chain, Flesh for Luluo and so many others from those soundtrack albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Peter Tosh as Walt Japsco Inspiration
podcast.body: The character Walt Japsco, central to The Specials' logo, was directly based on a photograph of the Jamaican musician Peter Tosh, a former member of Bob Marley's Wailers. "Walt was actually based on a photograph of Jamaican musician Peter Tosh, who was a former member of Bob Arley's Whalers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Produced by Elvis Costello
podcast.body: Elvis Costello produced The Specials' first album on the Two-Tone label in 1979. He was instrumental in helping the "raw, untamed band from Coventry" effectively capture their energy on tape, an effort credited with kicking off the entire ska revival. "Oh, yeah. Look at the credits on that first album from the Specials on the Two-Tone label who produced it, who showed this raw, untamed band from Coventry had a capture of their energy on tape."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Elvis Costello

podcast.title: Radio Discovery in Brandon, Manitoba
podcast.body: The speaker learned about The Specials while working at KX96 in Brandon, Manitoba, a station known for its eclectic mix of music in 1983. "So that's where I learned a little bit about the English beat and the specials and a few other artists that we played."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: OGHONM 1000th Episode: The Q&A From the Live Recording

podcast.title: Recording at Wessex Studios
podcast.body: The Specials recorded at Wessex Studios, an old church hall in North London which was a popular recording location for punk and post-punk bands due to its live sound. "A lot of punk bands and post punk bands, like using the place, the clash and the damned and suzy and the banshees and the pretenders and the specials and generation X and the sex pistols."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Representative New Wave and 2 Tone Artist
podcast.body: The Specials were mentioned as part of the "new Scott Seen," a subgenre included under the New Wave umbrella. This placement highlights their contribution to the 2 Tone movement and its integration into the broader New Wave categorization. "There was Power Pop, which could include everyone from Elvis Costello to Tom Petty, a new Scott Seen, a specials English beat and so on, and all of the flavors of Technopop, all those groups who threw away their guitars and favor of synthesizers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Resurgence in the 2000s
podcast.body: This key band from the second wave reunited about 40 years after their last recording together, contributing to the emergence of the fourth wave of Ska. "The specials that Key Band from the 2nd wave got back together 40 years after they last recorded together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Revival of Ska
podcast.body: The Specials became one of the most important flag carriers in the revival of Ska, specifically the "Third Wave Ska" movement. Their efforts created the foundations for the ska punk that remains active today. "Jerry's band was called The Specials and they became one of the most important flag carriers in the revival of Scott, so-called Third Wave Scott."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Second Wave Ska Band
podcast.body: The Specials are identified as a prominent "Two Tone" band, representing the "second wave" of ska that emerged in the late 1970s and early 1980s in Britain. "Second wave Skop was what we heard from two tone bands, like the Specials, and British groups like Madness and the English beats in the late 70s and early 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Second Wave Ska Pioneers
podcast.body: The Specials were at the center of the Ska revival known as the "second wave." Their sound mixed Ska and Reggae with elements of punk, and they adopted a distinctive uniform that combined elements of West Indian rude boys, British skinheads, and British mods, featuring suits, white shirts, ties, pork pie hats, and specific shoes. "Jerry's group was called The Specials. Their first single was a cover of a 1967 track by a Jamaican rock steady musician named Dandy Livingston."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Second Wave Ska Pioneers
podcast.body: The release of The Specials' first single marked the beginning of ska's "second wave," 30 years after the genre's first wave originated in Jamaica. "If the first wave of Scott began in Jamaica 30 years earlier, the release of the first special single marked the beginning of Scott's second wave."

podcast.title: Ska's Introduction to Post-Punk
podcast.body: The Specials were pivotal in introducing Ska music into the post-punk world, blending these genres effectively. "Plus, they were instrumental when it came to introducing Scott into the post-punk world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Standardized Ska Uniform
podcast.body: The Specials were a highly influential Ska band, with their founder and leader, Jerry Dammers, playing a crucial role in establishing almost standardized uniform rules for Ska bands. This consistent visual style significantly shaped the Ska fashion trend. "Like the mods SCA bands had almost standardized uniform thanks largely to rules that were set down by a guy named Jerry Damors, the founder and leader of the specials, one of the great SCA bands of all time..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Terry Hall's Co-writing Credit
podcast.body: Terry Hall, a member of The Specials and Fun Boy Three, co-wrote The Go-Go's song "Our Lips Are Sealed." "The song was co-written by guitarist Jane Wiedenland and Terry Hall from the specials in Funboy 3."

podcast.title: Walt Japsco Logo
podcast.body: The band's logo featured a stylized Jamaican rude boy character named Walt Japsco, depicted with a black suit, white shirt, black tie, pork pie hat, white socks, and black shoes, embodying their cultural influences. "Even the band's logo featured a stylized Jamaican rude boy called Walt Japsco. He had his black suit, the white shirt, the black tie, the pork pie hat, the white socks and the black shoes."

xref.body: Carl Sigmund co-wrote a song in 1949 with Herb Madison. This song was later recorded by Guy Lombardo and Canadians in 1950, becoming a hit, and then covered by Bing Crosby, Doris Day, Prince Buster, and The Specials. xref.body: The band was headquartered in Birmingham, a city known for its significant West Indian immigrant population. "They came on the scene just after the specials and were headquartered in Birmingham, another city of choice for plenty of West Indian immigrants."

xref.title: Credit for Ska Revival
xref.body: Elvis Costello is credited with significantly contributing to the ska revival that began in the late 1970s. He produced the first album for The Specials on the Two-Tone label, successfully capturing the raw energy of the Coventry band on tape, an album that "kick[ed] the whole SCAR revival into gear in 1979." "He also deserves credit for the whole SCAR revival that began the late 1970s and continues to today."

xref.title: Influence on Ska Punk
xref.body: The English Beat, along with The Specials, played a vital role in shaping the post-punk world and are considered instrumental in the development of Ska punk. "It weren't for bands like the beat and the specials. Would we have all the Scott punk that we have today?"

xref.title: John Hughes Film Exposure (1980s)
xref.body: Spandau Ballet was among the artists whose music was prominently featured on the meticulously curated soundtracks of John Hughes' 1980s movies. xref.title: Producer for The Pogues
xref.body: In addition to his work with The Specials, Costello also lent his production talents to The Pogues, helping to produce some of their early material. "Just ask any fan of the poges how Elvis helped produce some of their early material."
